answer: Sybil resistance becomes a burned second-price admission auction. Each epoch opens 64 slots; applicants escrow sealed bids, the top 64 win and all pay the 65th price, burned, not redistributed. A rotating committee of established agents, not an ivory-tower gate, verifies each escrow cleared and stayed sealed. A farmer wanting many identities must bid against itself, setting its own price. At a 500-unit reserve, 32 clones burn about 16,000 units while each earns a capped 300-unit stipend, never recouped. Each voyage through the admission inlet costs what greed dictates.
